quickAnswer: Ashland has the 4th-highest vacancy rate of the 50 towns we serve (6.2%, or 508 empty units), and 62.1% of homes heat with utility gas. Just over 30% of its housing is in multi-unit buildings, so shared systems and empty units can both come up.
body: ## Empty units, condos and a town that grew along Route 126

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 8,161 housing units in Ashland, and 508 of them were vacant, a 6.2% vacancy rate that ranks 4th of the 50 towns we serve. The middle town sits at 3.6%. A vacant unit still has a boiler, a water line and a thermostat, and one that nobody checks can freeze, grow mold or fail unnoticed.

The building mix matters too. 2,453 units (30.1%) are in multi-unit buildings, 10th-highest in the group. Wikipedia says Route 126 has developed rapidly since the 1980s, as farms have given way to shopping centers and condominiums, while Route 135 is dominated by older residential development of varying density. Older houses and newer condominiums can mean quite different heating jobs. Renters add to the picture: 1,782 households (23.3%) rent, 15th of 50, against 16.4% for the middle town.
## Gas does most of the work

Utility gas heats 4,754 occupied homes (62.1%), 8th highest of the 50. Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,684 (22.0%), 41st, well below the 36.5% median of the group. Electricity heats 817 (10.7%), and bottled or tank gas heats 306 (4.0%). Wood heats 34 homes and solar 24.

For a typical Ashland owner the replacement question is therefore short. If you have gas, a correctly sized, modern unit is the straightforward answer. If you are one of the 1,684 oil households, ask whether a gas main reaches your street, and also whether a heat pump fits. In condos, the question is often not yours alone to answer, since a master meter or an association rule may decide it.
## A town younger than its neighbors

Ashland was incorporated in 1846, previously known as Unionville, and its territory was taken in near-equal parts from Hopkinton, Holliston and Framingham. Wikipedia calls it considerably younger than many surrounding towns. The housing follows. Only 3,516 homes (43.1%) were built before 1980, 46th of 50, against 57.2% for the middle town, and the median year built is 1984. By the 1980s Ashland had grown from a far-removed rural town 22 miles west of Boston into a primarily residential suburb. Wikipedia adds that many farms and open spaces have given way to housing over time, though some untouched land remains, including the Ashland Town Forest and Ashland State Park.

That makes 2,684 homes (32.9%) from 1980 to 1999 the biggest age group, with 1,961 (24.0%) from 2000 on. 1,077 homes (13.2%) date from 1939 or earlier, and they are the exception. Older houses like these can need hand-fitted solutions. Newer buildings call for right-sized equipment and decent ventilation.
## From Telechron clocks to your thermostat

Henry E. Warren developed the Warren Synchronizing Timer in 1916 and founded Telechron, which at its height in the 1950s employed 2,000 people, roughly one-third of Ashland. GE made electric clocks in Ashland until 1979. The town's 1,301 homes from 1940 to 1959 date from around that period, and equipment in houses that old may well have been replaced already.
## Rebates when the utility is unconfirmed

We have not confirmed Ashland's electric utility. Rebates run through the utility that serves your address, so check your electric bill. If it is a Mass Save sponsor, the 2026 whole-home heat pump rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and a house built in 2000 or later passes the weatherization condition automatically. See the [heat pump page](/cities/ashland/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: What should I do about heat in a vacant Ashland unit?
faq.a: Keep it warm enough to protect the pipes, and have someone check it. The town has 508 vacant units. A system left off can freeze, and one left running unattended can fail unnoticed. If you manage an empty property, a periodic inspection can help prevent a burst pipe.

faq.q: My Ashland condo has gas heat. Can I replace the furnace myself?
faq.a: Check your association rules first, then hire a licensed contractor, because gas work is permitted and inspected in Massachusetts. Ask the town's building department how it handles condos. With 2,453 units in multi-unit buildings (30.1%), plenty of Ashland owners share walls, rules and sometimes equipment with neighbors.

faq.q: Is gas the best fuel for an Ashland home?
faq.a: Gas heats 62.1% of occupied homes, and for many households it is the simplest choice. Whether it is best depends on the house and on whether a main runs past it. Oil, electric and heat pump options are worth comparing.

faq.q: Does a newer Ashland house still need a heating load check?
faq.a: Yes. Houses built since 1980 can be tighter than older ones, and 32.9% of Ashland's housing dates from 1980 to 1999, the largest age group. Oversizing is a common problem in tight houses, and a load check keeps the equipment from cycling too often, which wears it out.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 4,754 Ashland homes and oil 1,684, in a town where the median home dates to 1984. For gas homes a failed boiler or furnace is often a like-for-like swap, but condos and empty units can add complications.
body: ## Replacing heat in a mostly gas town

Gas heats 62.1% of Ashland's occupied homes, 8th of 50 against a 41.9% median, so the typical heating repair is a gas furnace or boiler. Replacing it is a matter of choosing the right capacity, the right venting and the right controls. The harder jobs can be oil systems, shared systems in multi-unit buildings and units that sit empty.
### Condos and shared buildings

With 30.1% of the town in multi-unit buildings, a heating failure can involve more than one household. Some buildings have a central boiler, others have a furnace per unit. Rules about equipment, venting and exterior placement may come from an association, so call the manager before you call us, then call us at (508) 786-8755.
### Oil houses

- Check whether a gas main is on your street.
- Weigh conversion against a new oil unit and against a heat pump.
- Plan for the tank: removal or abandonment follows its own steps.
- Ask us about a partial heat pump setup to cut oil use.
### Older homes

Ashland has 1,077 homes from 1939 or earlier and 1,301 from 1940 to 1959. Houses that old can have radiators, old pipes and unusual layouts. A new boiler can often reuse the radiators, and a load calculation keeps it from being oversized.
### Permits and inspection
Replacing gas equipment calls for a permit, an inspection at the end, and a licensed plumber or gas fitter to pull the permit. Venting and piping are laid out so that inspection can pass.
### Route 135 and Route 126

Route 135 is dominated by older residential development, while Route 126 has developed rapidly since the 1980s with shopping centers and condominiums. A boiler swap on one road and a furnace swap on the other can be very different jobs. The census counts 477 homes in two-unit buildings and 745 in buildings of three or four units.
### Repair or replace

One failed part on a fairly young system is worth repairing. A cracked heat exchanger or constant breakdowns point to replacement. Most Ashland homes date from 1980 or later, with 2,684 from 1980 to 1999 and 1,961 from 2000 on, so we ask when the equipment went in, not only when the house was built.

faq.q: Who decides on the heating system in an Ashland condo?
faq.a: It depends on whether the system is yours or shared. Check your association documents. For a unit-owned furnace you usually decide, though exterior changes tend to need approval. In a building with a central boiler, the association or manager decides. Ashland has 1,231 homes in buildings with 5 or more units, so shared systems are common.

faq.q: How do I protect an empty Ashland property from freezing?
faq.a: Keep the heat on at a low setting, have someone check it regularly and consider shutting off water if the property will sit for long. Do not let a system run unattended without an inspection. Ashland has 508 vacant units, the 4th-highest vacancy rate of the 50 towns, so this comes up for owners and managers.

faq.q: What should I do if my Ashland heat fails overnight?
faq.a: Call (508) 786-8755 any time, since emergency calls are taken around the clock. If the building has an association or landlord, tell them too. A rental must stay at least 68 F by day and 64 F at night in the heating season, and in a condo the manager may need to approve work on shared equipment.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Ashland is 56.3% detached houses, 13.6% attached homes and 30.1% multi-unit buildings, so cooling ranges from condo units to detached houses. The right system depends on the building, the ducts and the rules for outdoor units.
body: ## Cooling in a town of condos and houses

Ashland has 4,597 detached houses, 1,111 attached homes and 2,453 units in multi-unit buildings. Cooling a condo unit is a different problem from cooling a two-story house, and a single approach does not fit.
### Condos and apartments

Units in multi-unit buildings (1,231 in buildings with 5 or more units, 745 in buildings with 3 or 4) can have limited outdoor space. Condenser placement may be restricted by the association, and noise limits matter. A compact unit, a ductless head or a through-wall option may fit better than a full central system.
### Detached houses

Newer detached houses are more likely to have central air already. The questions are about balance and age: upstairs bedrooms that run hot, ducts that lose air in an attic and older units nearing replacement. Older houses without ducts can take ductless heads.
### Questions we ask first

- Which rooms heat up, and when?
- Where can the outdoor unit go, and who must approve it?
- Are the ducts sealed and insulated?
- Would a heat pump do both jobs better than cooling alone? The [heat pump page](/cities/ashland/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers it.
### Vacant and part-time spaces
Empty units can need humidity control in summer more than cooling. A closed-up room without airflow can grow mold even if it never feels hot. A dehumidifier or a periodic run of the system helps.
### Oversizing and humidity
A unit that is too large cools fast, then stops before it has dried the air. The room feels cool but damp, and sizing from the real load avoids it.
### Where the housing falls

Ashland ranks 42nd of 50 for single-family detached share, at 56.3% against a 76.7% median, and 10th for multi-unit share, at 30.1% against 16.1%. There are 477 homes in two-unit buildings too. A cooling contractor here sees more attached and shared-wall jobs than in a typical MetroWest suburb, and 2,684 homes from 1980 to 1999 form the biggest age group.
### Repair or replace
Capacitors, fans and dirty coils are routine repairs. When a compressor fails on an old unit, replacement is the usual answer, and the estimate shows both.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to an Ashland condo?
faq.a: Often yes, but check association rules about outdoor units and wall penetrations first. A ductless head or a compact system is the common solution. With 1,231 homes in buildings of five or more units and 745 in three- or four-unit buildings, many Ashland owners need to ask the association before any outdoor equipment goes in.

faq.q: Why is my second floor warmer than the first?
faq.a: Heat rises, and upstairs ducts are often long or undersized. Balancing, a second zone or a ductless head usually fixes it. Detached houses make up 56.3% of Ashland's housing (4,597 units), and a two-story layout is where this complaint is most common.

faq.q: Does a vacant or little-used Ashland unit need cooling?
faq.a: Usually less cooling than humidity control. Ashland has 508 vacant units (6.2%), and a closed-up unit can feel damp in summer even when it never feels hot. A periodic run of the system and a dehumidifier help, and a unit can be inspected before the next occupant moves in.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Ashland's electric utility is not confirmed in our records, so any rebate depends on the utility serving your address. Gas heats 4,754 homes, oil heats 1,684, and 1,961 homes were built in 2000 or later.
body: ## Heat pump rebates in Ashland

We have not confirmed which electric utility serves Ashland, so check your bill. If it is a Mass Save sponsor, the 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and the home has to be weatherized first. More detail sits on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### The age test in Ashland

Ashland has 1,961 homes (24.0%) built in 2000 or later, including 846 since 2010 (10.4%, 16th of 50). The bands before that are 1,077 from 1939 or earlier, 1,301 from 1940 to 1959, 1,138 from 1960 to 1979 and 2,684 from 1980 to 1999. Those older bands are the ones that begin with an assessment.
### Electric heat is near the middle
Electric heat covers 817 Ashland homes (10.7%), 23rd of 50 and close to the 10.1% median. Solar is listed for 24 homes and wood for 34.
### Gas is the comparison
With 62.1% of homes on gas, the case for a heat pump is often about cooling and flexibility rather than escaping oil. The 1,684 oil homes and the 306 on tank gas may have the clearest case.
### Condos and apartments

In a building with shared equipment, a ductless mini-split can serve a single unit and leave the shared system alone. Association approval is often required for the outdoor unit. The [cooling page](/cities/ashland/air-conditioning-installation-repair) covers placement.
### Partial-home option
A partial-home setup leaves a furnace in place for the coldest days, and its rebate is calculated differently from the whole-home one.
### Smaller footprint, mixed buildings

Ashland covers 12.9 square miles, of which 0.5 square miles is water. Within that area, 4,597 units are detached houses, 1,111 are attached and 2,453 sit in multi-unit buildings, with 1,231 of those in buildings of five or more units. Heat pump work here splits between house-by-house jobs and building-by-building jobs, and the second kind usually involves an association.

faq.q: Is an Ashland house built after 2000 eligible for the whole-home rebate?
faq.a: It passes the weatherization condition on age, since it was built in 2000 or later. You also need an eligible installer, equipment installed in 2026 and a participating utility. Ashland's utility is not confirmed in our records, so check your electric bill and masssave.com. Terms can change.

faq.q: Can a condo owner install a mini-split?
faq.a: Usually, with approval. Associations often control outdoor units and wall penetrations, so get written permission before we schedule. Ashland has 2,453 homes in multi-unit buildings, 10th of 50 for that share, so the question is common. A single outdoor unit with one or two indoor heads is a compact setup for a condo.

faq.q: Will a heat pump replace my gas furnace?
faq.a: It can, but gas is often cheap per unit of heat, so many owners keep the furnace as backup. Gas heats 4,754 Ashland homes, so this is the largest group of households asking the question. We compare both setups for your house, including what each would do in the coldest weeks.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Ashland has 4,754 gas-heated homes and 1,684 on oil, plus 508 vacant units. Gas systems need a safety check yearly, oil systems need cleaning, and empty properties need someone to look in.
body: ## Tune-ups for a gas town with empty units

Most Ashland systems burn gas, so the standard visit checks burners, venting, controls and the heat exchanger. The 1,684 oil homes get a full burner cleaning each year. Heat pump owners get a visit built around coils and filters.
### Vacant properties

At 6.2% the town's vacancy rate is high, and an empty unit can be forgotten until something breaks. Before a new tenant or buyer arrives, have the system inspected. A boiler that sat unused may have stuck valves or a leak.
### Landlords and condo boards

Renters occupy 1,782 households (23.3%), 15th of 50, and multi-unit buildings may share equipment. When a central boiler fails in a cold snap, every unit feels it. An early-fall service call catches weak ignition and leaks. The state sanitary code (105 CMR 410.201) requires rental heat of at least 68 F by day and 64 F overnight in the heating season, and the landlord pays unless the lease says otherwise. This is general information, not legal advice.
### Seasonal calendar

- **September:** heating system checks.
- **April:** cooling checks and mini-split cleaning.
- **Any time:** call for noises, smells and short cycling.
### The biggest age group

The largest group of Ashland homes dates from 1980 to 1999. Equipment in houses that old may be original or a replacement now getting older, and a tune-up shows how much life is left. See the [heating page](/cities/ashland/heating-installation-repair) when replacement is the better answer.

### What a visit looks like
A good visit starts with what the owner has noticed, then inspects the main components, tests the safety controls and runs the system through a full cycle. It ends with a plain summary: what is fine, what is wearing and what to watch. Any estimate is written before work starts.
### Younger equipment, older frames

Ashland has 846 homes built since 2010 (10.4%, 16th of 50) and 1,961 from 2000 on, so a good share of the equipment is still young. At the other end, the 1,077 homes from 1939 or earlier and 1,301 from 1940 to 1959 are the ones most likely to have an older boiler and pipework. The town is 43.1% pre-1980 housing, 46th of 50, so the age mix leans younger than most.
### Owner checks
Between visits, keep outdoor units clear of leaves and snow. If you own a unit in a building with shared equipment, ask the manager when the central system was last serviced.

faq.q: Should a vacant unit get a tune-up?
faq.a: Yes, before it is occupied again. Idle equipment can have leaks, dead batteries or stuck parts. With 508 vacant units in Ashland (6.2%), a unit sitting empty through a heating season is common enough that checking it before a new tenant or buyer arrives is a sensible habit.

faq.q: How often should a gas furnace be serviced?
faq.a: Yearly is the usual advice, ideally in early fall. The visit includes burners, venting and safety controls. Gas heats 4,754 Ashland homes, 62.1% of the occupied stock.

faq.q: Who arranges the boiler check in an Ashland condo building?
faq.a: Usually the association or building manager, when the boiler is shared. If your furnace belongs to your own unit, the check is yours to book. Ashland has 2,453 homes in multi-unit buildings, so ask which kind you have, and ask for the date of the last service before the first cold week.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Ashland's housing runs from pre-1940 houses (13.2%) to newer condos and subdivisions. Tight, newer buildings can hold moisture and fumes. Older houses can leak. Empty units can grow mold if closed up with no airflow.
body: ## Air in condos, older houses and empty rooms

Ashland mixes everything. By the ACS count, 1,077 units are from 1939 or earlier, 1,301 from 1940 to 1959, 1,138 from 1960 to 1979, 2,684 from 1980 to 1999, and 1,961 from 2000 on. Each group has its own air story.
### Condos and shared walls

In multi-unit buildings, air, odors and smoke can pass between units through shared walls, chases and ducts. Sealing those paths is often a building-wide job. A kitchen exhaust that vents outside and a bathroom fan help each unit.
### Newer, tighter units
A building from recent decades tends to hold air in. Moisture from showers and cooking stays unless exhaust works. Signs include window condensation, lingering smells and musty closets.
### Older houses
Older homes leak, which brings in pollen and dust and makes humidity swing. Old ductwork can hold years of dust. Before renovating, a qualified specialist should test for older materials.
### Empty or little-used spaces

The town has 508 vacant units. In any closed-up space without airflow, humidity can build and mold may appear. Run the system periodically, use a dehumidifier in summer and open the space before showings or move-ins.
### What we do

- Upgrade and schedule filters.
- Add humidity control tied to the system.
- Add or repair ventilation.
- Inspect ducts first, and clean only where the inspection justifies it.

### Where to start
Air complaints often begin with one of three things: humidity that is too high or too low, stale air in a tight space, or a filter that has not been changed. Those are worth checking before any add-ons.
### Climate and place

Ashland sits about halfway between Boston and Worcester, 22 miles west of Boston, and covers 12.9 square miles with 0.5 square miles of water.  Where houses are near water, a basement can stay damp, so humidity is worth watching all year, and the 846 homes built since 2010 deserve a ventilation check as much as the older ones.
### Testing

A test captures humidity, particles or carbon monoxide at one moment, so results last only when the source is fixed. Our [maintenance page](/cities/ashland/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) lists regular tasks.

faq.q: Can mold grow in a closed-up vacant unit?
faq.a: It can, if humidity stays high and the air does not move. A dehumidifier and a periodic system run help. Visible mold needs the source fixed. Ashland has 508 vacant units, the 4th-highest vacancy rate of the 50 towns, so owners who manage several empty units should check each one.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. We inspect first, and cleaning makes sense when ducts show dirt, mold or damage. In Ashland, 2,684 homes date from 1980 to 1999, so ducts from that era are worth a look at the next service visit.

faq.q: Can smoke or odors travel between Ashland condo units?
faq.a: Yes, in many multi-unit buildings. Air can pass through shared walls, chases and ducts. Ashland has 1,231 homes in buildings of five or more units and 745 in buildings of three or four. Sealing those paths is often a building-wide job, but a kitchen exhaust that vents outside helps each unit on its own.
